28. When a person puts a lactometer into the milk, the whole part of the narrow stem sinks into the milk. What conclusions
can be drawn from this event?
Ans:- When the whole narrow stem of a lactometer sinks into the milk, the following conclusions can be drawn:
1. The milk is less dense than normal or has low solids (like fat and proteins).
2. Since the lactometer floats according to the density of the liquid, sinking of the stem indicates that the milk is diluted
or of poor quality.
In short, the milk is lighter or thinner than expected, so the lactometer cannot float normally.

1. What is the condition for an object to sink in water? State any two conditions. The cross-sectional
area of piston A1 and A2 is 50 cm³ and 0.2 m² respectively How much load can lift in piston A2 if 250
N force is applied on piston A1?
Ans:- Conditions for an object to sink in water:
1. The density of the object is greater than the density of water.
2. The weight of the object is greater than the buoyant force exerted by water.
